title: Common Lime: Ancient Lindens You Can Visit
meta_description: Groningen's oldest tree is one of these. Six common limes mapped across Dutch, Belgian and Finnish cities, most of them the last of a vanished row.
intro: Groningen's oldest tree is one of these, about 340 years old at a farmhouse called De Rollen, and so is the peace tree Antwerp planted on its Grote Markt on 3 September 1994. Common lime is a hybrid of Europe's two wild limes, and it took over the north as the tree you plant in rows: along canals, up drives, around squares. Most of the ones here are what is left of a row. Utrecht has a canal stretch named Onder de Linden, under the lindens, in the 17th century, and out at the Uithof a linden that went into the ground around 1750 when the land around it was farmland. The veteran at Clingendael in The Hague is the last member of a row that stopped being one long ago. Helsinki's is the thickest park lime in Finland, on an island in the city's harbour.
